Implementation Plan

Planning ref: `orchestrator/project-8598` @ `5c7fdf9472b310a1f43428177b84d5606ca00935` (integration branch mismatch: false). The default branch was read only for comparison. `scripts/tg_helpers.sh` is identical on both refs. Only `tests/test_tg_helpers_cleanup.py` differs: it is on this branch, and the matching script change is not.

## Files likely to change
- `scripts/tg_helpers.sh`
- `tests/test_tg_helpers_cleanup.py` (one small additional test; existing assertions unchanged)

## Scope and automation wiring
Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends curl_gh_api
Scope-mode justification: This issue restores the script half of #8600 and #8598's cleanup-side contract. The tests in `tests/test_tg_helpers_cleanup.py` and `changelog.d/8600-tg-cleanup-snapshot-retain.md` are already on the branch; the code is not. The plan covers every required item (snapshot-first, trusted author, exact markers, checked delete, keep-on-transient with a breaker, phase validation, plain-curl fallback). It goes no further because the issue's files_touched and acceptance cover only the cleanup contract. Boil the Lake: the one complete-but-cheap addition is a shared private worker, so both cleanup functions get the same fix with less code than patching each one. It adds no dependency and no external interface. §6 order (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed) puts closing the comment-DELETE injection first. Store-side author trust (`tg_store_msg_id` / `tg_store_phase_msg_id` picking which marker to append to) is a separate requirement that this issue does not list, so it stays out (see D6 and the warning below).

- **New or existing code:** this changes existing code only. There is no new script, no new workflow step and no new env var.
- **Entry points (unchanged):** existing callers keep running it.
  - `.github/workflows/plan.yml` (`tg_cleanup_phase_msgs ... "clarify"`)
  - `.github/workflows/implement.yml` (`tg_cleanup_phase_msgs ... "plan"`)
  - the orchestrator poller completion path (`tg_cleanup_msgs`)
- **Long-running supervisor:** none.
- **DB work:** none.
- **`docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`:** no entry needed.

## Functions or modules to implement
All of these go in `scripts/tg_helpers.sh`. Follow the file's existing style: tabs, opening brace on a new line, `# ---` banner comments. Every new code path must be safe under the callers' `set -euo pipefail`:
- Use `x=$((x + 1))`, never `((x++))`.
- Guard every command substitution with `|| { ...; }`.
- Never let a failing `[ ] && ...` be the last command of a function.

1. **Module state (after the double-source guard, before the functions).**
   - Phase pattern constant: `_TG_PHASE_PATTERN='^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$'`. It accepts `clarify`, `plan` and `plan_review`, and rejects `Plan`, `plan:1`, `clarify.*` and `a b`.
   - Identity cache globals: `_TG_GH_IDENTITY_STATE=""` (`""` | `resolved` | `unresolved`) and `_TG_GH_IDENTITY_LOGIN=""` (lower-cased).
   - Assign the globals unconditionally at source time so an inherited environment value cannot pre-seed a trusted login. Do not export them.
   - I grepped these names across scripts, tests and `.github/`; none is in use.

2. **`_tg_valid_phase <phase>`.** Returns 0 when `[[ "$1" =~ ${_TG_PHASE_PATTERN} ]]`. Prints nothing.

3. **`_tg_resolve_gh_identity`.**
   - Call it directly, never inside `$(...)`, so the cache persists for the whole process.
   - If `_TG_GH_IDENTITY_STATE` is non-empty, return 0.
   - Otherwise, read the attempt count from `GH_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (default 5) and cap it at 2 (minimum 1). Call:
     `GH_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS="${cap}" curl_gh_api -s --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: token ${GH_TOKEN}" -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.v3+json" "https://api.github.com/user" 2>/dev/null`
     The URL must be the last argument: `tests/test_tracking_comment_cap.py`'s harness reads `${@: -1}`.
   - Extract the login with jq: `if type=="object" and (.login|type)=="string" and (.login|test("\\A[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,38}(\\[bot\\])?\\z")) then (.login|ascii_downcase) else empty end`.
   - **On success:** set state `resolved` and store the lower-cased login.
   - **On failure** (non-zero exit from the call, HTTP error, transport error, unparsable reply or bad login): set state `unresolved` and print once per process:
     `::warning::Telegram tracking: could not resolve the GH_TOKEN identity; only github-actions[bot] tracking comments are trusted`
   - Always return 0.

4. **`_tg_delete_msg_checked <msg_id>` (new; the contract test calls this name).**
   - Prints nothing.
   - Returns 0 without calling anything when the bot secret, chat ID or `msg_id` is empty. That matches the old `tg_delete_msg` "nothing to do" outcome.
   - Calls `curl -s --max-time 10 -w '\n%{http_code}' -X POST "https://api.telegram.org/bot${TG_BOT_SECRET}/deleteMessage" -d "chat_id=${chat_id}" -d "message_id=${msg_id}" 2>/dev/null`.
   - Returns 1 on:
     - a non-zero curl exit (transport error);
     - a status that is not 3 digits;
     - HTTP 429 or 5xx;
     - a body that is not a JSON object with a boolean `.ok`, unless the status is 400.
   - Returns 0 on:
     - HTTP 400, whatever the body;
     - `.ok == true`;
     - `.ok == false` (permanent: "message to delete not found", "can't be deleted", or another `ok:false`).
   - Split the reply with `${resp##*$'\n'}` (status) and `${resp%$'\n'*}` (body). Use no temp files.

5. **`tg_delete_msg <msg_id>` (same signature).** Body becomes `_tg_delete_msg_checked "${msg_id}" || true; return 0`. That is exactly one deleteMessage call with `--max-time 10`, and it always returns 0.

6. **`_tg_cleanup_tracking_comments <issue_num> <phase-or-empty>` (new shared private worker).**
   - **a. Validate the issue number** with `[[ "${issue_num}" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]`, otherwise return 0 with no calls. This hardens the input; callers already pass numeric IDs.
   - **b. Resolve the identity** with `_tg_resolve_gh_identity`. It runs before the first page read, which matches the call order `test_markers_on_every_page_are_deleted` expects.
   - **c. Take the snapshot.** Starting at `page=1`, loop:
     - Read the page:
       `page_json=$(curl_gh_api -s --max-time 30 -H ... -H ... "${api_base}/${issue_num}/comments?per_page=100&page=${page}")`
     - If the read fails, print the existing warning and `return 0` (nothing deleted):
       - phase-less: `::warning::Failed to fetch issue comments for cleanup (issue #N, page P); aborting cleanup`
       - phase: `::warning::Failed to fetch issue comments for phase cleanup (issue #N, phase X, page P); aborting cleanup`
     - Get the count with `jq -er 'if type=="array" then length else error("not an array") end'`. If that fails, print the warning below and `return 0`:
       - phase-less: `::warning::Unparsable issue comments page for cleanup (issue #N, page P); aborting cleanup`
       - phase: `::warning::Unparsable issue comments page for phase cleanup (issue #N, phase X, page P); aborting cleanup`
     - Append that page's trusted records (item 7) to a local `records` string.
     - Stop when the count is 0 or below 100; otherwise `page=$((page + 1))`.
     - Nothing is deleted inside this loop.
   - **d. Act on the records.** `tg_ready` is true when both `TG_BOT_SECRET` and `_tg_chat_id` are non-empty. Read the records with `while IFS=$'\t' read -r cid ids; do ... done <<< "${records}"`:
     - Re-check each record in shell with `[[ ${cid} =~ ^[0-9]+$ && ${ids} =~ ^[0-9]+(,[0-9]+)*$ ]] || continue`.
     - If `tg_ready`, split the IDs with `IFS=',' read -r -a`. For each ID:
       - If 3 or more transient failures in a row have happened, count the ID as skipped and keep the comment.
       - Else if `_tg_delete_msg_checked` succeeds, reset the in-a-row counter.
       - Else count a failure, add 1 to the in-a-row counter and keep the comment.
       - Keep trying the comment's remaining IDs after a failure (the test expects 23 to be tried after 22 fails).
     - If the comment is kept, count it as kept. Otherwise delete it with `curl -s --max-time 10 -X DELETE -H "Authorization: token ${GH_TOKEN}" -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.v3+json" "https://api.github.com/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/comments/${cid}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`.
     - When `tg_ready` is false, delete every comment (current behaviour).
   - **e. Report.** If any comment was kept, print exactly one warning per call (`<sfx>` is `""` or ` (phase X)`):
     - no skipped IDs: `::warning::Telegram cleanup kept K tracking comment(s) on issue #N<sfx>: F message ID(s) hit a transient Telegram failure; the next cleanup retries them`
     - skipped IDs: `::warning::Telegram cleanup kept K tracking comment(s) on issue #N<sfx>: F message ID(s) hit a transient Telegram failure (S more not tried after 3 failures in a row); the next cleanup retries them`
   - Return 0.

7. **Record extraction (jq, inside item 6c).** Pass `--arg login "${_TG_GH_IDENTITY_LOGIN}"` and `--arg phase "${phase}"`. The filter:
   - Iterates `.[]` and keeps only objects where `.id` is a positive integer, `.body` is a string and `.user` is an object with a string `.login`.
   - Trusted author:
     - `$login != ""`: `(.user.login|ascii_downcase) == $login`.
     - Otherwise: `.user.login == "github-actions[bot]" and .user.type == "Bot"`.
   - Binds `.id as $cid`, then captures with Oniguruma `\A ... \z` anchors. Never use `^`/`$`: they match at line boundaries, which reopens the multi-line injection.
     - general: `\A<!-- tg_(?:cleanup|phase:[a-z][a-z0-9_]*):(?<ids>[0-9]+(?:,[0-9]+)*) -->\z`
     - phase: `"\\A<!-- tg_phase:" + $phase + ":(?<ids>[0-9]+(?:,[0-9]+)*) -->\\z"`. Concatenating `$phase` into the regex is safe only because the phase was validated first; say so in a code comment.
   - Emits only `"\($cid)\t\(.ids)"`, never the body.

8. **`tg_cleanup_phase_msgs <issue> <phase>` and `tg_cleanup_msgs <issue>`.** Keep the names, signatures
